system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## 0. How to read the Seller's package

The cover note says that clauses marked **[STANDARD]** have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides," are "FINAL," and should not be re-opened. It asks us to review only items marked [OPEN]. **No item in the package is marked [OPEN].** If we accepted that framing, nothing would be reviewed at all.

These labels are the Seller's negotiating position, not an agreed record. I have reviewed every position on its merits. **Please confirm with your principals whether anything was in fact agreed at principal level.** I have seen nothing showing that it was. Even where a headline number was discussed, the drafting around it (carve-outs, scope and interaction with disclosure) is plainly not settled.

The "market context" preamble is partly accurate. A 10–20% cap and roughly 1% basket are within range **for general warranties.** The Seller then uses that to justify applying the same limits to title, tax, indemnities and fraud, which is not market.

The Disclosure Letter is dated as at **22 September 2026**. It is now 5 November. Every factual item below (Bluefen consent, Riverlark, Ironquay payment, the DD-006 investigation) needs an update.

---

## 1. Limitation package: the core structural problem

The individual numbers are negotiable. The real danger is the **combination** of three things:
- limitations applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- title and capacity warranties folded into the general regime
- broad disclosure and buyer-knowledge provisions

Together, these would cap, time-bar and largely neutralise every remedy we have, including for the specific known problems.

### 1.1 Cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m
- This is acceptable **for general warranties only**, possibly with a push to 25–30% if no W&I policy is being placed.
- **Carve-outs required:**
  - title, capacity and fundamental warranties: capped at 100% of price
  - tax warranties and tax indemnity: 100% of price
  - specific indemnities (see below): separate caps or uncapped
  - fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment: uncapped
  - leakage, price adjustment, Debt and covenant breaches: not subject to the cap

### 1.2 De minimis / basket (cl 12.2): AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only
- The basket is about 1.04% of price, which is at the top of range, and the "excess only" (deductible) structure favours the Seller.
- **Push for:**
  - a **tipping** basket (first-dollar recovery once crossed) at around 0.5% (AUD 120k)
  - a de minimis of around AUD 10k
  - related claims aggregated for de minimis purposes
  - thresholds not to apply to title, tax, specific indemnities or fraud

### 1.3 Time limits (cl 12.3/13)
- 18 months for general warranties is arguable. **Push for 24 months** so that two audit cycles post-Completion are covered.
- The proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" is a catch-all that captures tax, title, indemnities and fraud. **Reject it.** Limitations should apply only to Warranty Claims (general) unless expressly extended.
- **Tax:** at least 5 years (ideally 7), to sit beyond the standard ATO amendment periods.
- **Title/fundamental:** 7 years, or the statutory limitation period.
- **Specific indemnities:** tailored periods, for example Privacy 3–4 years and IP 6 years.

### 1.4 Title / fundamental warranties on general caps "for administrative simplicity"
- **Reject outright.** Title to 100% of the shares is the thing we are paying AUD 24m for. A AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month window on title is not market for a share sale.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- **Carve out:**
  - fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its officers
  - specific indemnities
  - tax covenant
  - leakage and price-adjustment claims
  - Seller covenants (conduct of business, completion deliverables)
- Non-reliance clauses in NSW will not fully exclude Australian Consumer Law s18 misleading or deceptive conduct claims. However, they are evidentially damaging to us, so the fraud and misrepresentation carve-out still needs to be express.

---

## 2. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2)
- **Reject general disclosure.** The standard should be **fair disclosure**: specific, with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and the warranty affected.
- The data room should be disclosed only to the extent matters are fairly and specifically disclosed in the Disclosure Letter. At minimum, require a fixed, indexed and archived (USB/hash) copy as at a stated date.
- Public records should be limited to defined searches (ASIC, PPSR, court) conducted on stated dates.
- **No disclosure against** title/fundamental warranties, the tax covenant or specific indemnities.
- DL 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable in principle, but it must not dilute the specific indemnities.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- As drafted, the clause covers the Buyer, its advisers and anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. That is an extremely broad anti-sandbagging clause. In effect, every disclosed DD issue becomes unrecoverable.
- **Push for:**
  - an express pro-sandbagging clause (Buyer's knowledge does not prejudice claims), **or** as a fallback
  - limiting the clause to the *actual* knowledge of named Buyer individuals of matters *fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter*, excluding advisers and constructive knowledge.
- **Key consequence:** whatever the outcome on 8.3, the known issues in sections 3–9 below **cannot be left to the warranties.** They need specific indemnities, CPs, price deductions or retention. W&I insurers will also exclude known matters, which is a further reason for this approach.

---

## 3. Bluefen (cl 3 / 6.3): about 30% of revenue

**The Seller's position is internally inconsistent.** The update says the consent is "addressed." The Disclosure Letter (item 2) says no final written consent has been provided and there is no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.

The Seller proposes "reasonable endeavours" and to treat the CP as satisfied on mere delivery of "written consent." That would let a conditional or qualified consent satisfy the CP.

**Push for:**
- a CP requiring unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably)
- evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied
- no amendment of Bluefen terms, pricing or term as the price of consent
- an obligation on the Seller to use **best / all reasonable endeavours**
- Buyer-only waiver of the CP
- a long-stop date with a Buyer walk right

**Consider:**
- a warranty and specific indemnity, or an earn-out / price adjustment, if Bluefen terminates or materially reduces volume within 12 months on change-of-control grounds
- a retention or escrow linked to this risk

---

## 4. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): about AUD 3.2m outstanding

A release "following Completion" is incompatible with a debt-free / cash-free deal. The facility has a change-control clause (8.1). Completion itself may trigger default or acceleration while security over Company assets remains in place.

**Push for:**
- the facility amount treated as **Debt**, repaid from the purchase price at Completion under the funds flow
- a payoff letter from Riverlark confirming the exact payout figure and per-diem
- a deed of release delivered **at** Completion
- PPSR financing change statements and discharge of any registered or mortgage security, lodged at or immediately after Completion under an undertaking
- confirmation of whether Riverlark holds **security over the shares themselves** (relevant to title, section 9)
- break costs and fees treated as Debt
- release and payoff deliverables listed as Seller Completion deliverables

---

## 5. Completion bonuses (DD-005): AUD 420,000 excluded from funds flow

The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller." However, the **Company** is the obligor under the bonus arrangements. If they are not deducted, the Buyer bears them after Completion. The Disclosure Letter also leaves open payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.

**Push for:**
- the AUD 420k **plus** employer on-costs to be treated as Transaction Costs / Debt and deducted from price, or paid by the Seller with PAYG withholding through Company payroll funded by the Seller
- on-costs to include payroll tax, superannuation (whether these bonuses attract the super guarantee needs to be confirmed on the actual terms), PAYG and workers' compensation
- if any amount is paid before Completion, treatment as Leakage
- a specific indemnity for any shortfall or related claims, including bonuses that later vest under "continued employment" conditions
- the funds flow to itemise these amounts

---

## 6. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1 / DD-004, DD-010)

Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials transfers **only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.** DD-010 shows AUD 180k still open. Unless and until that is paid, the Company may not own the SOW3 IP. An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers the debt but **not the real risk**, which is loss of ownership of IP that may be embedded in the product.

**Push for:**
- before or at Completion: payment of all SOW3 fees, evidenced by bank confirmation, plus Ironquay's confirmation of receipt
- an executed confirmatory **assignment deed** from Ironquay, including moral rights consents for individual contributors
- making this a CP or Completion deliverable
- a specific IP indemnity covering:
  - third-party claims
  - costs of re-development or licensing
  - business interruption
  - with the indemnity outside the basket and general cap, a 6-year period and not subject to disclosure or buyer knowledge
- IP warranties (ownership, non-infringement) not to be qualified by DL item 4
- technical due diligence on how much of the core platform derives from SOW3 materials

---

## 7. DD-006 export / privacy incident

The Seller describes this as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The facts disclosed are:
- a download link sent to an unintended external email address
- about 1,240 records of personal information
- access, scope and notification obligations are all unknown

Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must carry out a reasonable and expeditious assessment of a suspected eligible data breach, generally within 30 days. The incident predates 22 September, so that window has likely passed. We need to know whether an assessment was completed and whether the OAIC and affected individuals were notified. The civil penalty ceilings were substantially increased in 2022. There may also be contractual breach-notification obligations to customers (check the Bluefen contract specifically).

**Push for:**
- an immediate information request covering:
  - the forensic report
  - access logs showing whether the link was opened or downloaded
  - recipient confirmation of deletion
  - the NDB assessment record
  - any OAIC or customer notifications
  - cyber insurance notification
- a pre-Completion covenant to complete the investigation with Buyer oversight and to make any required notifications
- a **specific indemnity** for all losses from the incident, including regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, notification and remediation costs, customer claims and contract losses
- the indemnity to sit outside the basket and general cap (or have a separate cap), with a 3–4 year period and no disclosure or buyer-knowledge defence
- a retention or escrow if the investigation is still open at signing
- the privacy and data security warranties to remain unqualified by DL item 6, other than for the specific facts disclosed

---

## 8. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011): 3 × AUD 110k

These are three **related** renewals of identical amounts, and the Disclosure Letter says to read them together for timing and scope. That pattern raises the question of whether a single commitment was split. One possibility is that this was done to stay below a conduct-of-business consent threshold or an internal approval limit.

**Check:** the SPA conduct-of-business threshold, and whether any of these were entered into after signing or exclusivity.

**Push for:**
- copies of all three contracts, with dates, term and termination rights
- confirmation of who approved them
- if not ordinary course, or if entered in breach of the conduct covenants: treatment as Debt or a price adjustment, or a specific indemnity
- tightening the conduct covenant so that related or aggregated commitments count towards the threshold

---

## 9. Title (DD-012)

A share register on its own is not adequate evidence of title. The Disclosure Letter concedes that the Buyer has not verified it.

**Push for:**
- full title and capacity warranties, capped at 100% of price with 7+ years (see section 1.4)
- cross-check of the register against ASIC records
- a PPSR search against the Seller and over the shares
- confirmation that there are no options, convertibles, ESOP entitlements or rights of first refusal
- original share certificates (or lost-certificate indemnity), signed share transfers and any required releases (including any Riverlark share security) as Completion deliverables

---

## 10. Other items

- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller's characterisation (notification only; the assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale) **must be verified by us.** We should review the change-of-control definitions in each document. Deliverables: lease notification served at Completion, plus a warranty that no third-party consents are triggered other than as disclosed.
- **Tax and IP "settled under the general regime":** Reject. We need:
  - a separate tax covenant / indemnity for pre-Completion tax, capped at 100% of price, with 5–7 years and no disclosure defence
  - IP warranties preserved, with the Ironquay indemnity as set out in section 6
- **Funds flow:** This must itemise the Riverlark payoff, bonuses and on-costs, Transaction Costs, any Ironquay payment, and any retention amounts, all reconciled to the debt-free / cash-free price mechanics.
- **Retention / escrow:** Given the open Bluefen, DD-006 and Ironquay items, propose a retention (for example 10–15% of price for 18–24 months) or a W&I policy plus a specific escrow for known matters, since W&I will not cover them.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer push-back |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Framing ("FINAL", [STANDARD]) | No review needed | Not agreed; full review. Confirm what principals actually settled |
| 2 | General cap | 20% for everything | 20–30% for general warranties only. Carve out title, tax, indemnities and fraud |
| 3 | Basket / de minimis | 250k deductible / 25k | ~120k tipping / ~10k, with aggregation |
| 4 | Time limits | 18m, applied to all Claims | 24m general; tax 5–7y; title 7y; indemnities tailored |
| 5 | Title / fundamental | Same as general | 100% of price, 7y, no disclosure |
| 6 | Limits / non-reliance | All Claims | Carve out fraud, indemnities, tax, leakage, covenants |
| 7 | Disclosure | General data room and public records | Fair, specific disclosure only; none against fundamental, tax or indemnities |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Includes advisers and "discoverable" matters | Pro-sandbagging; fallback is actual knowledge of fairly disclosed matters |
| 9 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent | Hard CP, unconditional consent, cl 11.3 satisfied, Buyer walk right, revenue protection |
| 10 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release after Completion | Repay from price at Completion; payoff letter, deed of release, PPSR discharges |
| 11 | Bonuses AUD 420k | Seller matter, not in funds flow | Deduct plus on-costs as Transaction Costs / Debt; indemnity |
| 12 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 fee | Pay before Completion; confirmatory assignment as CP; uncapped IP indemnity |
| 13 | DD-006 privacy incident | Immaterial | Urgent information request (NDB status); covenant; specific indemnity; retention |
| 14 | Sandbar 3 × 110k | Ordinary course | Contracts and approvals; check threshold-splitting; Debt / indemnity; tighten covenant |
| 15 | Title evidence | Share register | ASIC and PPSR checks; full deliverables; fundamental warranties |
| 16 | Tax / IP | General regime | Standalone tax covenant; preserved IP warranties |
| 17 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed | Verify change-of-control wording ourselves |
| 18 | Security for known risks | None | Retention / escrow; W&I won't cover known matters |

**Immediate next steps:**
1. Request a Disclosure Letter update brought down to the current date.
2. Issue an urgent RFI on DD-006, the Bluefen consent status, Ironquay payment and the Riverlark payoff figure.
3. Confirm internally what, if anything, was agreed at principal level.
4. Instruct the mark-up on the basis above.

This analysis is based only on the Seller's summary positions and Disclosure Letter. The underlying DD documents and full SPA text should be checked before the mark-up is finalised.
=== END ADVICE ===
